title: Lesson 6: Faith at Work and School
description: Most of your waking hours are spent at work or school, your 2nd Space. Through Daniel's faithful life in Babylon, you will see how to follow Jesus where most of your week is spent and live so there is nothing to find but faith.

blocks.text: In the last lesson, you learned to share your story and the story of Jesus. That is the moment when a friendship built through prayer, listening, meals, and service becomes a conversation about hope. This lesson carries those same BLESS rhythms into the place where most of your week is spent: your job, your classroom, or whatever work fills your days. God does not send you there alone, and He does not stay behind when you walk through the door.

blocks.title: Faithful in Babylon
blocks.text:
When Daniel was still a young man, the armies of Babylon conquered Jerusalem and carried him far from home (Daniel 1:1-6). Babylon was the most powerful empire in the world, and it did not worship Israel's God. The king gave Daniel a new name, enrolled him in a three-year school to learn the language and books of Babylon, and trained him to serve in the royal court.

Daniel did not get to choose his workplace, but he did choose how he would live in it. He studied hard, and God gave him unusual skill and understanding (Daniel 1:17). He also drew a quiet line. When he was served food from the king's table that he believed would defile him before God, he respectfully asked for another way. God gave him favor with the official in charge (Daniel 1:8-9).

Decades later, Daniel was an older man serving a new king named Darius. He had worked so faithfully that the king planned to put him over the whole kingdom. Jealous officials went looking for something to use against him and came up empty. They "could find no ground for complaint or any fault, because he was faithful, and no error or fault was found in him" (Daniel 6:4). The only thing left to attack was his faith. So they talked the king into signing a law that for thirty days no one could pray to any god or person except the king.

When Daniel heard about the law, he went home, opened his windows toward Jerusalem, and knelt to pray three times a day, "as he had done previously" (Daniel 6:10). He was arrested and thrown into a den of lions. At dawn the king hurried to the den, and Daniel called out that God had shut the lions' mouths (Daniel 6:22). Then the most powerful ruler in the world sent a message across his empire telling people to honor "the God of Daniel, for he is the living God" (Daniel 6:26).

Daniel's story is not mainly about a brave man. It is about a faithful God who was already in Babylon before Daniel arrived. Daniel did not earn God's care by being impressive at work. He belonged to God first, and that belonging shaped how he worked, how he spoke, and how he prayed. The same is true for you. Before this lesson asks anything of you, remember that in Christ you already belong to God, and He goes with you into every place you spend your week.

6.1 - The people who watched Daniel every day searched for something wrong and found only faithful work and faith in God. What stands out to you most about how Daniel lived in a workplace he did not choose?
Your Three Spaces

Most of your life happens in three kinds of places. Your 1st Space is home and the people closest to you, like family and close friends. Your 2nd Space is work and school, where most of your waking hours go. Your 3rd Space is everywhere else: the gym, the ball field, the coffee shop, a party, or the stranger in line beside you.

It is easy to think of following Jesus as something that happens mostly at home and on Sunday mornings. If you count the hours, though, the 2nd Space is where much of your week is spent, which means it is also where much of your faith is lived and seen. For some people the 2nd Space is an office or a job site. For others it is a classroom, a hospital shift, a delivery route, or a home where you care for children or an aging parent. If you are between jobs or retired, your 2nd Space is wherever your days are given to steady work and service right now.

blocks.alt: Your Three Spaces. Jesus is Lord of every space. 1st Space: home and close friends. 2nd Space, the focus of this lesson: work and school, where most of your week is spent. 3rd Space: everywhere else, like hobbies, gatherings and strangers. In your 2nd Space: nothing to find but faith, from Daniel 6:4-5.

blocks.text: Here is a simple way to remember it. Draw three circles and put a star on the middle one. Home is your 1st Space, work and school are your 2nd Space, and everywhere else is your 3rd Space. Jesus is Lord of all three, and this lesson is about the one in the middle.
Your Work Matters to God

Work did not begin as a punishment. Before anything in the world was broken, God placed the first man in the garden "to work it and keep it" (Genesis 2:15). Sin made work hard and sometimes painful, but work itself is a good gift. Jesus spent most of His adult life working with His hands as a carpenter (Mark 6:3) before He ever preached a sermon.
Whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men, knowing that from the Lord you will receive the inheritance as your reward. You are serving the Lord Christ.

Paul first wrote those words to servants who had very little control over their work. He did not tell them their jobs were too small to matter. He told them every task could be done for Jesus. Filing a report, stocking a shelf, finishing homework, or changing a diaper can all become worship when you do it for Him. Your boss or teacher is not your only audience, and the Lord watches your work with a Father's delight, not a critic's frown.
6.2 - Where is your 2nd Space right now? Where does it feel hardest to follow Jesus there, and where does it feel most natural?
Nothing to Find but Faith

The officials who watched Daniel summed up his life this way: "We shall not find any ground for complaint against this Daniel unless we find it in connection with the law of his God" (Daniel 6:5). What a thing to have said about you by the people who work beside you. You can carry it in one short phrase: nothing to find but faith. Daniel's story shows three ways that phrase takes shape in a 2nd Space.

Faithful work. Daniel did his job so well that the king trusted him with more (Daniel 6:3). Showing up on time and being honest about your hours are ways of loving God. So are finishing what you start and doing good work when no one is checking, because your work serves real people. Faithful work is not about being the best in the room. It is about being trustworthy with what has been put in your hands.

Clean integrity. Daniel lived among people with very different values, and he stayed respectful without giving up what God had said (Daniel 1:8). Your 2nd Space will have its own pressures. It might be a shortcut on a test, a joke at someone's expense, a report that bends the truth, or a group that loves to complain about the boss. You do not have to be harsh or preachy to be different, because quiet and kind honesty stands out more than you might think.
In the same way, let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father who is in heaven.

Steady prayer. When the pressure came, Daniel did not invent a new spiritual life overnight. He simply kept praying "as he had done previously." The faith that carried him into the lions' den was built on ordinary days. You can pray on the drive in, before a hard meeting, between classes, or for a coworker by name while you wait for the copier. Small, steady prayers turn an ordinary workplace into a place where you walk with God.
6.3 - Which of these feels hardest for you right now in your 2nd Space: faithful work, clean integrity, or steady prayer? What would it look like to ask God for help with that this week?
Bringing BLESS to Work
God gave His people in Babylon a surprising instruction. Instead of hiding or giving up, they were to work and pray for the good of the city where they had been sent.
But seek the welfare of the city where I have sent you into exile, and pray to the LORD on its behalf, for in its welfare you will find your welfare.

Daniel's faithfulness opened a door no one expected, and a pagan king ended up telling his whole empire about the living God. God can use your faithfulness in the same way. The people you see every week at work or school are not interruptions to your mission. They may be the very people God has placed around you to hear about Jesus.

The BLESS rhythms fit right into your 2nd Space. Begin with prayer for two or three coworkers or classmates by name. Listen well when someone mentions a sick parent or a hard week. Eat with people by taking lunch with a coworker instead of eating alone at your desk. Serve by helping someone who is behind, without keeping score. When the moment is right, share your story and the hope of Jesus with gentleness and respect. Honor your workplace's rules and your employer's time as you do, because faith that is lived well usually opens more doors than faith that is pushed.

Maybe this lesson brings to mind times you have cut corners, lost your temper at work, or kept your faith hidden. Daniel's God is your God, and He is rich in mercy. Jesus was perfectly faithful in every place He ever worked, and in Him you are forgiven and fully loved. You do not live for Jesus at work to earn His love. You get to live for Him because you already have it, and His mercies are new every morning (Lamentations 3:22-23), including tomorrow morning in your 2nd Space.

blocks.title: If your workplace is not safe
content: Faithfulness does not mean staying silent while you are harmed. If you are being harassed, threatened, or pressured to do something illegal or clearly wrong, you do not have to carry it alone. Talk with a pastor or another trusted believer, use the proper reporting channels where you work or study, and get wise help.
If you are in immediate danger, call 911.

blocks.text: 6.4 - Write the first names or initials of two or three people in your 2nd Space. What is one simple way you could pray for, listen to, or serve one of them this week?
Lesson 6 Review

Your life unfolds in three spaces: home, work and school, and everywhere else. Jesus is Lord of all three, and your 2nd Space is where much of your week and much of your witness takes place. Daniel belonged to God in a workplace he did not choose, and the people watching him could find nothing against him but his faith. By God's grace you can live the same way through faithful work, clean integrity, and steady prayer, while you bring the BLESS rhythms to the people beside you. In the next lesson, you will see why living on mission meets real spiritual resistance and how God equips you to stand.
